cells.tense: The turning is recognized as the weight is carried, and the pen stays on the page.
cells.act: let the finished thing be the start of something
cells.ask: Give the piece of work that is nearly done its last step, then let whatever comes after it begin without you watching over it.
cells.core: Something is arriving now, and you are meeting it as it comes, not from three moves ahead. The weight of what has to be held here is real, and your body is set to hold it — not braced, not rigid, just sturdy enough to stay with what is actually here. When something reaches its end, you set it down whole. You let it be finished and stay open to what it becomes after. That is the art of this: closing a cycle without making the closing final. You can tell the difference between done and dead. Not many can. The work that has been waiting on its last step is asking for you now. Take it there, then step into what opens.
cells.sheetLine: You can finish a thing and still leave the door open.
cells.verb: Recognizing what is arriving now and turning to meet it
cells.place: Where you take the weight of what will not be set down

cells.tense: The future is being written before it arrives, and every draft of it is being carried at once.
cells.act: close the cycle and leave the door open for the next
cells.ask: Take a thread that is already over and close it — then stand in front of that closed door a while before opening the next.
cells.core: You are carrying currents that haven't happened yet. Tomorrow and the week after and the version of things you keep rehearsing are all held at once, and your body is taking the strain of futures that haven't arrived. It feels like being carried. It is. The current runs you instead of the other way. Somewhere in the middle of all that, you have lost track of which things are finished and which ones you are still holding open just in case. The weight is real and yours to set down. Take a thread that is over. Close it. Not because closing is safe, but because holding what is done is what leaves no hand free for what is coming.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying every tomorrow at once, and none have landed.
cells.verb: Recognizing what is arriving now and turning to meet it
cells.place: Where you take the weight of what will not be set down

cells.tense: You have stepped back from the wheel and the door you are still standing at is behind you.
cells.act: finish the thing that has been waiting on its last step
cells.ask: Find the project that is nearly done — truly nearly done — and take it the last step, in the world, not in your head.
cells.core: You have been holding yourself above the turning, standing back from the whole thing, waiting until it settles into a shape you can agree with. But the things that wanted to be done got left unfinished when you stepped away — the last step of something, the actual end of it — and they are still waiting. Your ability to hold what is heavy is present. It has simply been pointed at a fixed idea of how things should be rather than at what is here. The body you can carry the world with is the same body that can take one piece of work to its end. Not by pushing. By naming the piece that is nearly done and finishing it, in the world, this week. The wheel doesn't need you off it. It needs you on it with your hands on something real.
cells.sheetLine: You stepped off the wheel and the last step is still waiting.
cells.verb: Recognizing what is arriving now and turning to meet it
cells.place: Where you take the weight of what will not be set down

cells.tense: The turning is happening right now and it has not been claimed as yours to make.
cells.act: refuse the second thing so the first can have you
cells.ask: Choose where your attention goes this season, and turn down the other pull, so what you picked can have all of you.
cells.core: You do not realize yet that you are the one carrying this forward. When things land out of nowhere and you are surprised at how they turned out, you speak as if the current did it. But the weight was in your hands the whole time, and the turning you are meeting now is one you made, even if you didn't watch yourself make it. Your endurance has been holding the thing without a name attached to it. This is the moment to sign. Not to endure harder, but to decide — say which way this goes and let the direction be yours to keep. The shape your life takes from here will keep looking like something that happened to you until you write a direction into it. Let one thing have you.
cells.sheetLine: The turning is yours to make, and the pen is still down.
cells.verb: Recognizing what is arriving now and turning to meet it
cells.place: Where you take the weight of what will not be set down

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's being carried by the current, or standing at an old door, is about how they hold arrival rather than about the particulars of what is arriving. A reader could reasonably say the conditions in their life are doing the carrying, not their way of meeting it. The ask survives being wrong because finishing or choosing the one thing still teaches them how they meet what is next either way. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is any line that turns holding capacity into a verdict about how present they are.
